title: A reference course shows presentation only
statement: Let a reference course inform only interaction and presentation: it never proves a verdict, content correctness or grade fit, and none of its content, numbers or policies carry across.
detail: The Grade 5 reading release uses the Grade 3 player as a presentation reference, not as course authority, and copies none of Grade 3's story content, mascot language, passage chunking, vocabulary count or item policy (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/docs/GRADE_5_REVIEW_NOTES.qmd`, lines 9 and 28-31). Its instruction-review profile gives the reference the role of interaction and presentation reference only, lists criterion verdict, content correctness and grade appropriateness as what it may not prove, and admits a reference-course artifact only in a comparison note, never as verdict evidence (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/generated/instruction-review-profile.json`, lines 116-127 and 156). A Grade 7 BrainLift treats its neighbouring grades the same way: they are method templates, and their numbers are theirs (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g7-reading/releases/2026-07-26/artifacts/Grade 7 Reading - BrainLift.md`, lines 451-453).
